title: A Alibi for the Letter
premise: Quentin Brightwater, a retired detective who fled a career-ending scandal, has hidden behind the counter of her failing bookshop for three years, cataloging the town of Marrow Bay's secrets in a private ledger. When twin letters arrive—one confessing to a murder committed at last year's anniversary dinner, one promising that 'the witness will speak again'—she realizes the case she was forced to bury is resurfacing, and the witness everyone swears is dead may be alive and hiding in plain sight. As Quentin investigates outside the law with an unlikely found family of misfits, she uncovers that the town's most powerful family corrupted the original investigation, including her own testimony. At the anniversary dinner, Quentin exposes the killer and produces the living witness, choosing justice over the safety of invisibility and finally claiming Marrow Bay as home.
about_author: Coral Zhou is a former court stenographer who spent a decade transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about quiet people who keep dangerous records, from a house full of rescued typewriters.

chapters.title: Filed Under B
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In her cluttered bookshop, Quentin alphabetizes a secret ledger of town secrets when twin letters arrive in matching envelopes: one confessing to the death of Ada Voss at last year's anniversary dinner, one promising 'the witness will speak again.' Emotional beat: dread cracking open her carefully ordered invisibility.

chapters.title: The Confession That Doesn't Fit
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She compares the confession against her own buried notes from the Voss case and finds details only the true killer would know—yet the handwriting belongs to someone who was out of town that night. Emotional beat: the old instinct waking, and the guilt of having signed away the truth three years ago.

chapters.title: Regulars and Liars
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Quentin and Dev, the teenage shop assistant who reads everything on the shelves. Quentin quietly questions dinner guests while Dev notices which regulars avoid the mystery section since the letters came. Emotional beat: the first fragile threads of found family forming around shared suspicion.

chapters.title: The Voss Anniversary
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The wealthy Voss family announces this year's anniversary dinner will honor Ada's memory—and invites Quentin personally, a message from someone who knows who she is. Emotional beat: realizing her anonymity was always an illusion someone permitted.

chapters.title: Dead Women Don't Write Letters
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev traces the stationery of both letters to a defunct print shop and finds a living employee who saw 'the dead witness' buying paper last month. Emotional beat: terror and thrill as Dev realizes they're now inside the story.

chapters.title: What I Signed Away
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Flashback interwoven with present: the night three years ago when Judge Aldous Voss pressured her into recanting her testimony, trading her silence for escape from scandal. Emotional beat: shame curdling into resolve; power's corruption made personal.

chapters.title: The Witness in the Margins
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Following the print-shop thread, Quentin discovers the witness—Ada's housekeeper, presumed drowned—living under a new name, too frightened to testify because her son is held by debt to the Voss estate. Emotional beat: compassion overriding self-preservation; the stakes become someone else's freedom.

chapters.title: Glass Houses, Full Glasses
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Days before the dinner, the second letter-writer is found dead, staged as suicide, and the sheriff—a man in Voss's pocket—closes the case in hours. Emotional beat: grief and fury; the law itself revealed as the crime scene.

chapters.title: A Toast to the Truth
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At the anniversary dinner, Quentin plays the confession aloud, springs the trap that forces Judge Voss's son to incriminate himself, and reveals the housekeeper alive among the catering staff. Emotional beat: triumphant, terrifying exposure—the climax where invisibility dies.

chapters.title: Reshelved
chapters.summary: Dev's POV, closing with Quentin. With the Vosses indicted and the sheriff resigned, the bookshop fills with neighbors who finally see Quentin clearly; she burns the ledger page by page, keeping only Ada's name. Emotional beat: peace earned through courage—found family, justice outside the law, and a home no longer hidden.
